name: Counter Anchor
description: An Anchor program that keeps a count in an account.

intro.promise: You'll write a program that keeps a count in an account, and count with it on devnet.

steps.title: Counter account
steps.objective: Write initialize and increment around a Counter account
steps.learned: Keeping a count in an account

beats.text: Every Anchor program opens with the same two lines: the import and the program's id. They're routine, so I've written them.
A program keeps nothing between calls, so your count needs an account to live in. I've written `Counter` at the bottom: an account that holds one `u64` named `count`.

`initialize` creates the counter, so it needs three accounts: the `counter`, your wallet as `user` to sign and pay, and the System Program, which creates accounts. The counter sits at a program derived address (PDA), worked out from the word `counter` and your wallet, so a call can find it again. `space` is 8 bytes Anchor keeps for itself plus 8 for the `u64`. It's routine, so I've written it.

writes.block:
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct Initialize<'info> {
    #[account(
        init,
        payer = user,
        space = 8 + 8,
        seeds = [b"counter", user.key().as_ref()],
        bump
    )]
    pub counter: Account<'info, Counter>,
    #[account(mut)]
    pub user: Signer<'info>,
    pub system_program: Program<'info, System>,
}

beats.text: `increment` works on the same address, so it finds the counter you made. It marks `counter` as `mut`, because it will change it, and asks for your wallet as `user` to sign. I've written that too.

A program does its work in instructions: functions inside a module marked `#[program]`. Yours has two, `initialize`, which sets the counter up, and `increment`, which adds one and logs the new count. A program on Solana has no terminal: the only place it can write is the program log, which comes back with every transaction. You pick the line that adds one.

beats.question: Which line adds one to the count?
beats.right: Yes. `+= 1` adds one and stores it back in the account. I've put both instructions in the `#[program]` module, with a `msg!` that logs the new count.
why: Rust has no `++` operator, so this doesn't compile. Adding one in place is written `+= 1`.
That works out a new number and throws it away. The account's `count` stays as it was.
beats.hint: You want to change the stored `count`, not work out a new number. Which line changes it, in Rust?
beats.typed: That's the line. `+= 1` adds one to the stored count. I've put `initialize` and `increment` in the `#[program]` module around it.

beats.text: A deployed program is just code, and a transaction can't change it. Anything that has to last, like a count, needs a home of its own.

beats.question: Where does the count live?
options: In the program log, which the program reads back next time
In a variable the program keeps between calls
In the `Counter` account, at an address worked out from your wallet
beats.right: Yes. The program holds only code; the count is in the `Counter` account at that address. `initialize` creates it next.
why: The log is a printout that comes back with a transaction. A program can't read it later, so it can't hold the count.
A program keeps no variables between calls. What has to last goes in an account.
beats.hint: What did you deploy: code, or data?
beats.skipped: No problem. The count lives in the `Counter` account, not in the program. `initialize` creates it next.
